text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Strike today affects most of public sector.
- Defence Minister Mordechai met Arafat at Gaza crossing; Ross returns to Israel today.
- Concern over possible attempt by Palestinians and Kurds to attack Israeli target in Turkey.
- Netanyahu: the government will assist immigrants who claim to have lost money on way to Israel.
JERUSALEM POST
- Histadrut to escalate strike.
- Left, right MKs may abstain in Hebron no-confidence vote.
- Ross returns to seal Hebron deal.
- Homeless man dies from exposure.
- Finance Committee: Deficit must drop to 1.5% of GDP by 2001.
- Bank of Israel warns against rising tax burden.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu to strike leaders: You've lost your minds.
- President Ezer Weizman in India: I left here as a pilot and returned as president.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Strike has cost the economy 180 million shekels.
- Israel linked to satellite network to get early warning of missile strikes.
GLOBES
- Efforts to prevent deterioration of crisis between employers and striking workers.
